item.title: CAFA urges unified policies to grow Africa’s fashion economy to $500bn
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power. item.title: CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert. Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi. The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration. The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life. It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy. The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts. In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene. Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries. Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women. He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure. Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it. “In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said. He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return. item.title: ‘Thank you, Test Cricket’: Mohammed Shami retires from longest format of the game
item.description: NEW DELHI: Fast bowler Mohammed Shami has retired from Test cricket, closing a 13-year career in the longest format with an emotional message on Instagram on Friday night. The announcement came exactly 13 years after his Test debut. Shami first played for India in the format on 6 November 2013, against West Indies in Kolkata. “I am bidding farewell to the white jersey, but never to the memories associated with it,” Shami wrote. Recalling his first Test cap, he added: “When I wore India’s Test jersey for the first time, I had only one dream — to do something for my country. Since then, every wicket, every struggle, every injury, and every comeback has taught me something.” He described the format as far more than a place to play. “Test cricket has not just been a format for me, it has been a deeply special part of my life,” Shami further noted. “Today, with a heavy heart and countless beautiful memories, I am announcing my retirement from Test cricket.” — MdShami11 (@MdShami11) The 36-year-old thanked the people around him, from “every teammate, coach, family member, and the millions of Indians who supported me on this journey, and who kept their faith in me through both good times and bad.” He also named the BCCI and the Cricket Association of Bengal, his home association, for backing him early. “A sincere thank you as well to the BCCI and the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) for believing in my talent, giving me opportunities to grow, and playing a vital role in my cricketing journey. Your support and trust will always remain special to me.” Shami finishes with 229 wickets from 64 Tests, including six five-wicket hauls and best figures of 6/56. His last Test was the June 2023 match against Australia. In the same year he was the leading wicket-taker at the ODI World Cup, with 24 wickets in seven innings. He closed his message on a personal note. “Even though my final Test ball has been bowled on the field, the pride of playing for India will always remain alive in my heart. Thank you, Test Cricket.”

item.title: Chase Briscoe leads NASCAR Cup Homestead practice; Larson brushes wall and Reddick wrecks
item.description: Motorsport photo The one and only NASCAR Cup Series practice of championship weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway has concluded on Friday night, with Chase Briscoe sitting atop the speed charts with a 32.680s (165.238mph) lap. He beat Austin Cindric by 0.073s, while distant title challengers Denny Hamlin and Christopher Bell were third and fourth, respectively. Ryan Blaney rounded out the top five. Championship leader Kyle Larson was ninth, and found the wall several times as he worked the highest groove around the 1.5-mile intermediate track, suffering slight damage on the right-side of his No. 5 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet. He wasn't alone in brushing the wall, with Joey Logano among those who also got up into it during the session. Cindric also led five-lap averages, while his Penske teammate Blaney led 10, 15, 20, 25, and even 30-lap averages. "That's probably pretty excessive," said Larson about his wall contact after the session. "Yeah, I just didn't feel very good. I don't know, I didn't feel comfortable for the first few laps, and then I would feel okay, and then I just didn't have enough grip to run the wall like I needed to. I'll just have to kind of think about that and what I was doing wrong, and then listen to my teammates, kind of what they had to say about their cars. But just a disconnect and (lack of) comfort, I guess, from the first few laps to the end of whatever. I didn't get to run super long, but, I'm getting glued -- stuck in the wall. So, yeah, that was not a great practice, but I haven't really even gotten to dive into it yet." "I just didn't have enough grip." Hear from @KyleLarsonRacin following practice. https://t.co/GsIjLDCoqN — NASCAR (@NASCAR) November 6, 2026 Reddick pit road accident At the end of practice, there was an unusual incident as Tyler Reddick was attempting to perform a mock pit stop, but slammed into the back of a slowing Zane Smith at pit entry, spinning out and damaging the nose of his No. 45 car. Team co-owner Michael Jordan looked on from the pits, dismayed, and Reddick was visibly frustrated after climbing from the car. "Just sums up our year," said Reddick. "When we have something that's really solid, we find a way to screw it up. Me and Zane were both coming pit road hot, kind of almost at the point of no return. I realized he was really checking up big, and I saw that there was a car ahead, turning the garage. So, I'm guessing that's where all of our trouble started. You know, we were both coming in hot, so expecting to roll down pit road, and I couldn't tell who -- oh, 34 [Todd Gilliland]. Yeah, there we go. I was looking at the replay, but that's just what it felt like. You know, we were coming pit road hot, and he checked up, and I guess it was just cars coming in to turn into the garage ... it just sucks." item.title: ‘Stop playing games’: SEC reportedly considering luxury tax for schools that overspend on players
item.description: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The SEC might be borrowing an idea from professional sports. The conference is reportedly considering a luxury tax on schools that spend more on their players than the revenue-sharing cap allows. A working group of SEC athletic directors, university presidents, and general counsels has been discussing the idea for the past few weeks. The league could vote on it soon, with the hope of having it in place before football’s early signing period in December. The revenue-sharing cap Under the House v. NCAA settlement, schools are allowed to pay their athletes directly through revenue sharing, up to a set cap. That cap is $21.3 million for the 2026-27 academic year and will rise to about $22.2 million in 2027-28. Schools have found ways to spend beyond that, though. Much of the extra money gets routed through third-party NIL deals, which makes it hard for anyone to know what their competitors are actually paying. The SEC isn’t the only conference trying to rein that in. Last month, the Big Ten adopted a conference rule limiting its schools’ involvement in third-party NIL deals, ahead of the possible passage of the Protect College Sports Act in Congress. The PCSA would increase the amount schools can pay players directly by $27.5 million. It’s now unclear whether Congress will pass it after Tuesday’s elections. ‘People stop playing games’ According to ESPN’s Mark Schlabach and Pete Thamel, one formula the SEC is considering would gradually tax schools once they go over the cap. For example, a school could be taxed 1% for spending $1 million over the cap and 3% for spending $3 million over. The details are still being worked out, and some schools want to keep the penalty as low as possible. “Some schools want it to be where the penalty is as low as possible, so it’s cheap enough to where you’re more motivated just to pay it directly and report it, and everybody’s on the same page and people stop playing games,” a source said, via ESPN . The goal is to discourage overspending, while also giving schools a clearer picture of what everyone else is paying. The SEC also hopes it would cut down on the need for third parties to “wash” the money. “It’s a lot better if we all know what everybody’s doing right now,” a source told ESPN. “We’re living in this world where we have no idea what anybody’s spending. Agents can play you all day long because there is no general database. We’re starting to get some information, but there’s not enough transparency to know what people are really doing.” We’ll have to see whether or not the SEC actually moves forward with this plan. The post ‘Stop playing games’: SEC reportedly considering luxury tax for schools that overspend on players appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Bimbo Ademoye shines in dual roles
item.description: By Ammah Sarah Bimbo Ademoye is stepping into one of the biggest moments of her career as she takes on a dual role in the highly anticipated film,”The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives.” The actress is not only starring in the film, she is also serving as an Executive Producer, a move that shows her growth from screen star to power player behind the scenes. In the film, Ademoye plays the character Iya Femi, a role fans are already excited to see her bring to life. Sharing the news with her followers, Ademoye expressed her excitement about being part of the production, describing it as a special experience from start to finish. The film has already started making waves internationally. From Toronto to London, it has enjoyed screenings at two prestigious Oscar-qualifying film festivals, earning attention from global audiences and critics. Now, the excitement is moving to Africa. The film is set to celebrate its premiere in Africa November 29, an event fans across the continent have been waiting for. After the premiere, it will be released in Nigeria and other West African countries on December 4, and in the UK, USA, and Canada on December 11. item.title: Why Heat’s Erik Spoelstra ‘feels’ for Tim Hardaway Jr. amid limited minutes
item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Why Heat’s Erik Spoelstra ‘feels’ for Tim Hardaway Jr. amid limited minutes appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Golden State Warriors beating the Miami Heat on Thursday on the second night of a back-to-back, 120-100, the latter is still looking to find its groove with all its new faces such as Giannis Antetokounmpo , Klay Thompson , and others. As the Heat now fall to 3-6 on the season after the loss to the Warriors, one newcomer who has been struggling recently is Tim Hardaway Jr., as head coach Erik Spoelstra speaks on the matter. Hardaway was signed this offseason to bring dynamic shooting to the team and be an energizer off the bench, especially coming off a season with the Denver Nuggets where he received Sixth Man of the Year consideration, shooting 40.7 percent from deep. Through nine games in familiar territory in Miami, as he grew up in the city while his father played with the Heat for six years, Hardaway Jr. has averaged 5.1 points while shooting 28.6 percent from the field and 24.3 percent from three-point range. The minutes have been eye-opening, as while his role was a sure-fire to record double-digit minutes, the last two games say otherwise. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Heat’s Erik Spoelstra: “I feel for Tim right now” Playing seven minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Los Angeles Clippers and four minutes in the aforementioned loss to the Warriors, as rookie Ryan Conwell has been getting extended play recently. Hardaway is looking to get himself back in the rotation, as Spoelstra explains why it isn’t solely the guard’s fault. “I feel for Tim right now because it’s not really about him,” Spoelstra said, via The Miami Herald. “It’s not necessarily anybody in that second unit right now. We’re just facing some teams that have multiple ball handlers and point-of-attack guys. That was a good lineup for us yesterday when we had D. Mitch and Ryan out there together. It wasn’t really moving the needle for us tonight, so that’s just the way it goes sometimes.” At any rate, it remains to be seen what Hardaway’s role looks like with Miami as the next game comes on Sunday against the Sacramento Kings. item.title: Hamlin and Bell left with what could have been in NASCAR Chase
item.description: Motorsport photo Statistically, Kyle Larson has a 99.4 percent chance of winning the NASCAR Cup Series championship on Sunday at Homestead-Miami Speedway, leaving Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin at a combined .6 percent. In short, either of them coming back to win the Chase for the Championship would amount to the most improbable comeback in the history of a stock car season finale, so they are not holding their figurative breath. All Larson has to do is finish 28th on Sunday but that assumes he fails to score a single stage point as well. Each stage point he earns over the first half of the race lowers that bare minimum clinch spot by one. He could put the championship away prior to halfway by scoring eight stage points. In other words, a third-place finish in stage one ends the championship. Fourth and eighth over the first two stages ends it. So how much confidence does Hamlin have in his .3 odds? "I mean, I don't have any optimism," Hamlin said. "I don't. I'm here to try to have fun and try to win the race if possible, but I don't … I mean, there's obviously a chance you can win the lottery as well, but do you really count on that?" Bell added that he ‘doesn’t know what else to say,’ because the odds are the odds. Read Also: Kyle Larson sits alone on stage for NASCAR Championship Media Day How Kyle Larson can lose the NASCAR Cup championship at Homestead For Hamlin, this Chase for the Championship was especially frustrating because he entered as the top seeded contender and had four regular season wins. It was a championship he controlled from the summer through the Bristol Night Race. It's all he wanted after being two laps away from winning the championship last year under the final four format before a caution took that one away too. "I felt like last year was like a sudden death and this one was just a slow bleed, truthfully," Hamlin said. "I mean, that's really was how it was. I mean, I was in shock for 10 minutes after the checkered flag waved because I hadn't seen (Larson) all day and now he's suddenly ahead of me. "And then this year, through each playoff race, I'm on the way home just thinking, 'Gosh, it's alright though. We'll have to just make up for it next week.' And then we've just been trickling along and staying somewhat mathematically possible by being solid, but this one was definitely a cut to the wrist and we just watched it bleed." While Larson has taken control of the championship with his three playoff wins and second most stage points earned over the past nine races, Bell and Hamlin also endured mistakes that could have made this a lot closer. “Ultimately, I think whenever we got into The Chase, the 5 car had a pickup in performance, but I still think by the numbers, there have been guys in Toyota cars specifically that have been faster than them, but just we all shot ourselves in a foot one way or the other,” Bell said. item.title: Fixtures and standings as Nations Championship returns
item.description: The Nations Championship resumed on Friday with Ireland securing a 42-12 win over Argentina, as the battle for continental supremacy heats up. After three rounds of home games for southern hemisphere nations in July, the northern hemisphere teams are the hosts for the final three rounds. Ireland's win over Argentina moved them top of the standings in the north, but France and Scotland can move above the Irish with victories on Saturday. Six Nations champions France face Fiji on Saturday while Scotland - who are one point behind Les Bleus - hope to beat against New Zealand for the first time at Murrayfield on Saturday before games against Australia and Japan. Third-placed England have 10 points and play Australia - who are third in the southern standings - at Allianz Stadium on Sunday before taking on Japan and New Zealand. Ireland, who also have 10 points, face the challenge of taking on South Africa in the final round after playing Fiji in their second home game. Wales beat Fiji before losing to Argentina and South Africa in their opening three matches. Their home games are against Japan, New Zealand and Australia. Bottom-side Italy lost all three of their away games and face South Africa on Saturday. The Springboks beat England, Scotland and Wales at home in their opening three Tests to lead New Zealand on points difference. Rugby Union Weekly: Can England afford to lose to Australia? The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams will play each of the six in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures staged in July and another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six. On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. item.title: Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Still basking in the glow of her surprise 32nd birthday party, Toke Makinwa is taking her fans on a nostalgic trip back to where it all began. The Nigerian media personality and actress has announced plans to stage a live podcast of the first episode of her live show on November 21 in Lagos. Taking to Instagram to share the news, the former OAP wrote: “A little nostalgic trip down memory lane… We have come so far. I remember my very first episode. Let’s meet, let’s connect, November 21, in Lagos.” Her birthday on November 3 was anything but quiet. Friends and well-wishers pulled off a surprise party for the queen, and videos from the celebration showed her enjoying every moment with her circle. Though she admitted she wasn’t easily surprised, this time she dofed her cap for her friends. “I had the longest birthday blues, did not want to do anything on my birthday which is not like me and I am so thankful my circle did not listen,” she wrote. “She had two outfits and when everyone kept cancelling from coming to my house, I agreed to go to dinner at @maisonprivelagos. “I walked in totally surprised. I had the best dinner.” The post Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: What Major Changes Could Brewers Make After Championship?
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series last season, but will now have to get ready for next season. The Brewers have a chance to be more than just a one-and-done championship team. Almost all of their key players are under contract for next season and beyond, and they are a very young team that is expected to only get better. However, it's impossible to carry the same team into the next season. The Brewers may not be making many changes to their championship team, but some are coming. Infield Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The big question mark for the Brewers is Jake Bauers. He was extended a qualifying offer, but he was one of their best hitters last year, and losing him would be a huge change. Luckily for the Brewers, they already have their replacement in Andrew Vaughn, who was expected to be the starting first baseman before his injury, opening the door for Bauers. Vaughn being the starting first baseman all season would be a big change, but not necessarily a bad one. He has been great since joining the Brewers. As for depth at first base, the Brewers could look at prospects Blake Burke or Andrew Fischer. Fischer had a historic season in the minors, hitting 48 home runs. Outfield The Brewers' outfield is pretty cut and dry. Jackson Chourio and Garrett Mitchell will start every day. Sal Frelick and Luis Lara are expected to share right field. Lara is already signed to an extension, and Frelick played through a labrum injury last season. The two could make for great production in right field. Starting Rotation This is the group that will see the most changes for the Brewers, but in a good way. Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson will be the Nos. 1 and 2 in the rotation. Robert Gasser came on late in the year and looks like he will be the team's No. 3 going into the year. The Brewers also likely expect Kyle Harrison to revert back to form and he will surely be back in the rotation. Those four being in the rotation all year will be a big change from last season, but the biggest change will be Quinn Priester. Priester was great for the Brewers in 2025, really reviving his career. He underwent season-ending thoracic outlet decompression surgery this year and should be ready by the time the season starts. The Brewers' rotation is expected to be even better next season. Bullpen Here, the name to watch is Trevor Megill. He is one year away from free agency and could meet the same fate as Josh Hader and Devin Williams. The Brewers could trade him this offseason, pushing Abner Uribe into the closer role. Uribe is very capable, and Aaron Ashby would be the best setup man in baseball. As for other changes, the Brewers could look to add relievers in free agency. JoJo Romero and Antonio Senzatela are both free agents and played a big role down the stretch for the Brewers. item.title: No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey dominates No. 6-seed Iowa, 4-1, in Big Ten Tournament semifinals
item.description: No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey has a knack for fast starts. Entering Friday’s Big Ten tournament semifinal against No. 6-seed Iowa, the Terps had outscored opponents by 11 in the first quarter. By the time the first 15 minutes had elapsed on Friday in Columbus, Ohio, the Terps added two more goals to the aforementioned total. Maryland’s fast start set the tone for what turned out to be a 4-1 demolition of Iowa. Like the teams’ regular-season matchup a week ago, Maryland jumped on Iowa for a quick score. Despite failures on its first two penalty corners, Maryland maintained pressure and eventually broke Iowa’s tight defense. Jordyn Hollamon used a brilliant backhanded shot from the left wing to the top right corner of the cage to get the offense started five minutes into the match. 10 minutes later, the Terps made it two in the first frame. On an unconventional penalty corner routine, Babs van Hest received the insertion, rotated to her right and attempted a shot towards the near post. The ball immediately clanked off an Iowa defender and was redirected over the head of Iowa goalkeeper Julia Claessens to make it 2-0. The early explosion was eerily similar to last Friday’s matchup. In the first meeting, Maryland scored three times in the opening quarter and forced Iowa to switch goalies. While Maryland only scored twice this time around, the Terps still forced Iowa’s hand. When the second quarter began, Abby Johnson was in net for the Hawkeyes. “I think it was the way we got the penalty corners. We used some nice deflections in the shell area that got into people’s feet,” said head coach Missy Meharg. “I think we were super creative, and [the players] believed that they could pick up each other’s balls that they just tipped in [the net].” Iowa settled down in the second quarter, holding Maryland’s offense to two shots and one corner while generating transition offense. As the quarter wound down, Iowa’s attack was at its best with relentless pressure in the shooting circle. However, the Hawkeyes couldn’t find the net, as goalkeeper Alyssa Klebasko and defender Josie Hollamon teamed up to make a trio of big-time denials and keep the Hawkeyes scoreless heading into the break. Hollamon especially was on her game. On a pair of occasions in that sequence, Klebasko was slightly out of position, but Hollamon was there to stop the ball’s advancements and distribute it to her teammates, who cleared the ball away from danger. Maryland came out the aggressor in the second half, creating four set pieces off the bat. It took all four of those corners, but the Terps eventually found their third goal of the affair. Maci Bradford fed Ella Beach with a perfect centering pass, and the freshman tapped it home for her fourth goal in the last five matches. “She’s amazing,” Meharg said. “You can play her anywhere on the field, any way through the midfield, she can split seams and eliminate two people on reception going forward. She’s playing really good hockey.” Penalt

item.title: Las Vegas Raiders-San Francisco 49ers FEED Topic: Who gets more touches between Mike Washington Jr., Ashton Jeanty?
item.description: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak made headlines during last week’s game against the New York Jets. Not for himself, but a decision he made with Las Vegas’ backfield. Kubiak didn’t just switch the Raiders’ lead running back between rookie Mike Washington Jr. and second-year pro Ashton Jeanty; he turned Washington into the feature back with 25 carries and made Jeanty the third-down option with just two carries and three catches. Now, heading into the Week 9 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, the question arises of whether the workload split between Washington and Jeanty will continue . Some have speculated that Kubiak’s decision was punitive-based. Ahead of last week’s game, Jeanty gave the Jets ‘bulletin board material’ by saying that a few players on New York’s defense “don’t really want to tackle”. While the first-time head coach is still establishing his identity, he’s made it clear that he takes a ‘no-nonsense’ type of approach and doesn’t divulge much to the media to avoid situations like this. So, there’s reason to believe that the running back’s comments irked Kubiak and played a role in the former’s workload last Sunday. However, this Sunday will give us a better answer to see if the 25-to-2 (or 12.5-to-1) ratio of carries, or a similar type of split, continues. On Monday, the head coach indicated that the workload between the two backs could vary game to game. “I think it’s always a moving target,” he replied when asked if the Raiders will have a shared backfield moving forward. “See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And they’ve been changing at guard…That’s the NFL. “We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” Despite those comments, it’s hard to deny that the Raiders’ rushing attack did a better job of staying on schedule last week. Washington had 83 yards on his 25 carries, which comes out to 3.3 ypc. That’s pretty comparable to Jeanty’s 3.1 ypc for the season. But the rookie’s average was brought down by a handful of stuffed runs near the goal line. Also, Vegas’ EPA per rush was 0.11 points better last week than the team’s season average, and its success rate on the ground was 7.2% higher, per Sumer Sports . That being said, Washington’s lack of success in the red zone can’t be ignored. He’s averaging 1.2 ypc (17 attempts for 21 yards) inside the 20-yard line, per Sumer , and is viewed as more of a home-run hitter out of the backfield. Granted, Jeanty isn’t much better in the scoring area — 1.6 ypc (22 attempts for 36 yards) — but it is an improvement on a slightly bigger sample size. Also, he’s arguably the better option at getting the tough yards of the two backs. So, maybe Klint Kubiak’s formula moving

item.title: Buckeyes’ Ryan Day makes playoff admission that may concern Ohio State fans
item.description: The College Football Playoff selection committee placed the Ohio State Buckeyes at No. 12 in its first rankings of the season on Tuesday, Nov. 3, and on this week’s board that number lands one spot outside the field. The Boise State Broncos, ranked No. 25, hold the automatic bid for the highest-ranked Group of Five champion, which leaves Ohio State as the first team out. The Buckeyes got there with a 30-18 loss to the unranked USC Trojans on Oct. 31, the first time Ohio State has taken two losses before November since 2011. True freshman Luke Fahey made his first career start in that game because Julian Sayin is out with an injury to his throwing arm, suffered in a 19-15 win at the Indiana Hoosiers on Oct. 17. Ohio State coach Ryan Day has already said Sayin’s return is “not going to be next week or next month.” “No margin right now. There was a thin margin last week; now there’s no margin. We knew that when we saw the schedule. We saw what this stretch was gonna be like on the road and what was gonna come and coming back home and playing Oregon. We’re in it right now,” Day said on the Ryan Day Radio Show this week. Ryan Day knows what the #Buckeyes have to do: “To me, it’s just win.” @CBSSportsCFB https://t.co/R4xEd84BC9 — Bucknuts (@Bucknuts247) November 6, 2026 Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day yells during the NCAA football game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Nov. 22, 2025. Ohio State won 42-9. Can Ohio State win out with a freshman at quarterback? Four regular-season games remain: the No. 23 Oregon Ducks visit Columbus on Saturday, followed by the Northwestern Wildcats, the Nebraska Cornhuskers and the Michigan Wolverines. Ohio State’s six wins include Indiana, now No. 4 in the committee’s rankings, and No. 19 Iowa, and its two losses both came on the road. A 10-2 finish would put the Buckeyes in strong position for a spot in the 12-team field. At USC, Ohio State reached the red zone four times and came away with three field goals. Fahey finished 21 of 38 for 260 yards and a touchdown, and the Buckeyes did not find the end zone until the final minutes. “At the end of the day, once we get in a red zone, we have to be able to run the ball and then we have to be able to win one-on-ones on the outside and you know certainly that is something that is extremely frustrating,” Day said at his Tuesday news conference. Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches from the sideline during the first half of the NCAA football game against the Texas Longhorns at Ohio Stadium on Aug. 30, 2025. A win over Oregon would give Ohio State a third victory over a team in the committee’s top 25, and every loss by a team ranked above the Buckeyes opens room to climb before the next rankings come out on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Over the next four weeks, though, that plan depends on turning red-zone trips into touchdowns with a first-year quarterback taking the snaps. item.title: Nick Saban says 24-team College Football Playoff is ‘about the money’
item.description: Nick Saban was asked about the College Football Playoff’s planned move to 24 teams on this week’s episode of New Heights, the podcast hosted by brothers Jason and Travis Kelce. The seven-time national champion coach, now an analyst on ESPN’s College GameDay, did not need long to answer. “Too many. There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the national championship. So, what is the reason to actually do it? He’s got it. Yeah, but what you’re giving up, which is what I hate to see, is, you know, the SEC Championship Game playing the SEC Championship Game was a big thing to our players. It was a big thing to our fans. It was a tradition, and it was a great venue. I mean, there is only two teams that can play in a national championship, but more teams can play in those kinds of championship games, and there’s a lot of pride in winning the conference championship. And we’re going to give that up to have an extra game where the 24th team is going to play the ninth-best team. I’m not a big proponent of it. I think it minimizes the importance of the season,” Saban said. Ex Alabama head coach Nick Saban. (Credits – IMAGN) Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger first reported in October that the CFP had reached a deal with ESPN to double the field starting with the 2027 season, and ESPN reported days later that the sides had a handshake agreement, though the contract has not been formally signed. Under the format Dellenger laid out , conference championship games go away, the top eight seeds get byes, and seeds 9 through 24 open with on-campus games in the second week of December. Only one spot is reserved, for the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, with the other 23 coming from the committee’s rankings. ESPN is expected to pay about $350 million more for the expanded postseason, according to Dellenger’s reporting, and after the roughly $200 million in lost conference title game revenue comes off the top, about $150 million is left for the conferences to split. Big Ten and SEC schools would each net an estimated $2.5 million to $3 million a year. “There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the National Championship” Nick Saban is OUT on the 24 team playoff, so quit askin’ NEW EPISODE OUT NOW!!! https://t.co/aehwBp51Q7 — New Heights (@newheightshow) November 6, 2026 Does the data back Nick Saban’s 24-team argument? The 12-team era has produced two national title games, and the lowest seed to reach one was 10th-seeded Miami last January. The champions were No. 8 seed Ohio State in the first year and No. 1 seed Indiana in the second. Nothing seeded below 10th has played for the title. Last season’s final rankings show exactly who a 24-team field would have added. The 12 teams ranked inside the top 23 that missed the bracket were Notre Dame, BYU, Texas, Vanderbilt, Utah, USC, Arizona, Michigan, Virginia, Houston, Georgia Tech and Iowa. Eight of them had at least three losses, and Iowa had four. March 30, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Nick Saban answer quest

item.title: How the NHL is bringing the ski slopes inside Rice-Eccles Stadium
item.description: Signage for the National Hockey League’s 2027 Winter Classic is displayed before a press conference held by the Utah Mammoth and NHL at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Jan. 7, 2026. | Isaac Hale, Deseret News Outdoor NHL games count the same as every other contest — two points in the standings. But that’s the last thing people remember about events like the Winter Classic. NHL president of content and events Steve Mayer and his team have spent the last year devising the best possible game-day experience for fans at the New Year’s Eve game between the Utah Mammoth and the Colorado Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium. In an exclusive interview with the Deseret News, he laid out his plan. “What we’re building out is a bit of a winter wonderland,” Mayer said. “And there’s probably no better place to build that out than in Utah, given the proximity to the ski resorts. “We’re building out a ski resort on the field and in that stadium, and that’s sort of the overall look and feel for our game.” What does he mean when he says they’re building out a ski resort? He means they’re literally building an area to ski. There’s a large amount of open space between the rink and the stands, given the size disparity between a hockey rink and the football field that the stadium was built to house. The NHL is putting an actual, functioning cross-country skiing track in that space. The musician headlining the intermission show has yet to be announced, but the plan is for the artist to utilize the ski track while performing. Mayer’s team is also exploring the possibility of building either a ski lift or a mountain in the corner of the stadium, which he says is made possible because of the height of Rice-Eccles Stadium. In addition, the players will enter through a “ski chalet/cabin” and there will be a large fire pit to stay cozy. The other climate in the state of Utah will be represented in the form of red rock, just as it is in the game’s official logo . “Our goal is that when a fan not in the stadium — when a fan in New York City, in Miami, Florida, in Munich, Germany — tunes into the game, they know that we’re in Utah. ... It’s a showcase for Salt Lake City. This is our chance to show off that area to the world.” A big focus of Mayer’s team is to cultivate the perfect first impression for when walking into the stadium. The “wow” factor is an invaluable part of the experience. “Being in Utah, for us, is really exciting,” he said. “I mean, the backdrop is absolutely awesome. And that obviously is going to lead to how the field is designed and the activities that we’ll have around the game. “Our goal every one of these games is to have that fan who is in that seat when they walk into the stadium go, ‘Whoa. Wow. Like, this is cool.’ It’s that first impression that we work really hard on.” The rest of the game-day experience should be spectacular as well. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end shared that he “can’t wait” to share a milestone with his wife. Kelce is fresh off a solid performance. I start celebrating as that tree goes up.” Travis Kelce is ready for his first Christmas with Taylor Swift as husband and wife! The NFL star is part of Tommy Hilfiger’s holiday campaign, appearing alongside other brand ambassadors and tastemakers. “I’m excited for my first holiday as a married man,” Kelce said in a quote to Women’s Wear Daily. “I love all the old traditions and can’t wait to start some new ones. I start celebrating as that tree goes up.” In a video shared by Tommy Hilfiger, Travis says his perfect holiday includes “my mother baking blueberry muffins.” As for his festive attire, Travis says with a laugh, “You got any Tommy Christmas onesies somewhere?” ( : Instagram/Tommy Hilfiger) — ExtraTV (@extratv) November 5, 2026 The lead-up to their wedding sent the media and fans into a frenzy. She already watched one matchup this season at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs will play their next game on Sunday at home. They will host the New York Jets with their sights set on getting back on track and snapping their skid. item.title: Lions Coach Makes Emotional Jack Campbell Admission Amid His Scary Injury
item.description: Jack Campbell Getty Jack Campbell of the Detroit Lions Getty The past few days have been difficult for the Detroit Lions and everyone close to linebacker Jack Campbell, teammates and family alike. The All-Pro is currently battling a scary neck injury sustained in the Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. An uncertainty clouds his future in football, but the Lions fraternity believes he has the fighting spirit to bounce back. The Lions assistant head coach and safety coach, Jim O’Neil, talked about Jack Campbell today while talking to the press, where he applauded the linebacker’s fighting spirit, as concern grows over his future. “Thoughts and prayers, obviously, with Jack and his family as they’re going through what they’re going through,” Jim O’Neil said . “A lot of emotions in the game of football, and one emotion you kind of condition yourself not to let creep into your brain is fear. And then obviously, when Jack went down, I think everybody felt it. And it was a tough situation, but there’s no doubt Jack’s a warrior, and he’s going to come through it. He’s going to come through it.” Jack Campbell has been one of the key pieces of the Lions’ defense, and his shoes will not be easy to fill, but the franchise will be determined to honor the LB moving forward . Lions Rally Behind Jack Campbell As He Faces Difficult Road To Recovery What looked like a simple play became a concerning neck injury for Jack Campbell last Sunday. When he went to tackle the Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson, his head awkwardly hit the lower body, causing the injury. While the 26-year-old has been battling the injury alone, he has a lot of support from his Lions teammates and coaching staff, as coach Jim O’Neil insisted. Getty Jack Campbell of the Detroit Lions “And I think it’s awesome. I think it’s awesome how the team rallied behind him. I think it’s awesome how they’re going to play for him and how they’ve prepared like him all week,” O’Neil stated during the same press conference. “So again, thoughts and prayers with their family. I know they’ve got a long road to go, but Jack’s a monster. He’s going to come out of it.” Campbell was roped in by the Lions in the first round of the 2023 draft. Since his rookie year, the linebacker has played every regular-season game, featuring 51 games in his first three seasons. This season, he featured in 7 games, so the Week 9 Dolphins game will be the first time he will miss NFL regular-season action. With 57 tackles, he continued his great run from last season, so replacing him would be a challenge for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. Lions Face Crucial Test After Losing Two Linebackers To Injury Besides Jack Campbell, rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder also went down with a season-ending injury in the last game, so the Lions don’t have many options in the LB room. For now, the veteran Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes could be the favorite to be his replacement . He is a starter (6 starts this season) and has experience p

item.title: Stansfield enjoying altered role at high-flying Blues
item.description: Jay Stansfield's goal on Tuesday, Blues' third in their 3-0 home win against Millwall, was only his second of the season [Shutterstock] Birmingham City record signing Jay Stansfield may have only scored two goals so far this season - but the way Blues are playing, coupled with his own form, has him hoping that there are still plenty more to come. After his 12 Championship goals failed to prevent Blues being relegated in 2023-24, Stansfield then increased that number to 19 in League One to help win promotion when his loan signing from Fulham had been turned into a £15m move . He added 10 more in the Championship last season to help Blues finish 10th - and is now within one goal of becoming only the third Birmingham City player to reach 50 goals for the club in the past 40 seasons - to follow Paul Furlong (56) and Stansfield's former team-mate Lukas Jutkiewicz (69) in that respect. But he is now doing it in a very different role to when he first arrived at the club - and is very much enjoying playing as a foil to targetman August Priske, especially when, even without January signing Priske on the park, Max Bird set him up to score Blues' third goal in their early match-winning blitz at home to Millwall on Tuesday. That was Birmingham's fifth win in six games since the three-week international break - and they now head into Saturday's home test against Swansea City having overtaken the early Championship leaders as third plays fifth, with both teams on the same points. "We used the break to come together and work on a lot of things," Stansfield told BBC Radio WM. "And you can see the improvement of the whole team in general. The starters and the bench players." Triple injury boost for Swansea before Blues test Stewart hoping unlikely path leads back to top "The best teams are full of hungry players, raring to go," he added. "And everyone is in a good place. "It's important that other players are chipping in with the goals. All the players we've brought on have done well. And it's so good to have direct wingers like Liam Millar and Demarai Gray who look to score goals." Full-back Alex Cochrane got his second goal in successive games in the win over Millwall, before August signing Bird claimed his first. "Different people have been scoring, which helps us as forwards knowing someone else can step up and score," said Stansfield. "The last few games I've really enjoyed and I'm developing more and more. "Last season we were playing out from the back a lot, but now we're playing into a big striker in August. Our connection and understanding can only get better too. "I used to love in my academy days getting on the ball and making things happen. I like to peel off the shoulder and get balls played in behind, and last season I wasn't doing much of that. "Being the second striker and feeding off August, I've had some really good chances. As long as I'm getting chances, that's key. Now I've got one I can kick on."

item.title: Inside the Rams’ secret shadow boxing league that is bringing the team together
item.description: Referees, ranked contenders, a leaderboard, and even a commissioner are overseeing the entire operation. Welcome to the Los Angeles Rams shadow boxing league, where the competition is fierce, the trash talk is plentiful and the bragging rights might be worth more than the championship itself. Oh, and at the center of it all is the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year, who also happens to be the undisputed champion of the league. Instead of retreating into their phones between meetings, players are challenging teammates, laughing, talking trash and building relationships that extend beyond their position groups. Getty Images What initially started as a harmless way to kill some time between meetings has blossomed into a full-fledged locker room phenomenon, bringing players together during a season filled with injuries, adversity and enormous expectations. Rams linebacker Grant Stuard is the self-appointed commissioner, who has turned a childhood-style game into something resembling the UFC. “We thought it’d be cool to get some organization going and get a league started,” Stuard told the California Post in an exclusive interview Thursday. Stuard and teammate Matthew Caldwell helped establish a running leaderboard that now features a top 10, position-group rankings and honorable mentions. Even injured players have found their way onto the board. But at this point you’re probably asking yourself the same question we did: What exactly is shadow boxing? Despite its name, nobody is throwing any actual punches. Two players stand face-to-face. One points up, down, left or right while the other simultaneously moves his head in a direction, hoping to avoid looking where his opponent points. If the movements match, the attacker scores. Players alternate turns, attempting to anticipate each other’s reactions and string together successful moves. It’s part reflexes, part mind games and entirely addictive. Throughout the season, easily over half the Rams locker room has participated. And because NFL players apparently can’t compete at anything without turning it into its own organized sport, Stuard has established official rules. Ranked matches are best-of-three and require a witness or referee. Matchups involving the top three competitors require two officials. “If it’s a top-three ranked match, you need two refs,” Stuard explained. “You have to have some standards of what’s acceptable play.” The rankings operate similar to the UFC’s weight class rankings. An unranked player can challenge a ranked contender, and if the higher-ranked player accepts and loses, the leaderboard gets reshuffled. Throughout the past several weeks rankings 2-10 have been erased more times than a toddler’s Etch A Sketch, but one name has remained untouchable at the top of the leaderboard. Myles Garrett. The best defensive player in the NFL today is also the reigning, defending, and undisputed king of the Rams shadow boxing league. If and when the tournament takes place, Garrett’

item.title: Clippers’ Brandon Ingram Making Surprising Progress From Offseason Surgery
item.description: Los Angeles Clippers forward Brandon Ingram continues to make progress in his return from offseason Achilles surgery. He has returned to full contact 5-on-5 practices and is getting closer to a return. Getty The Los Angeles Clippers revealed a scary setback when forward Brandon Ingram underwent surgery that would stall his start to the 2026-27 season. It was revealed that Ingram underwent surgery to repair a right heel and a partially torn Achilles tendon in his foot, according to ESPN’s Ben Golliver. The news came four months after Ingram’s surgery, raising concerns for the Clippers after they traded for the 29-year-old during the offseason. Although recovery from a partially torn Achilles takes time, the team shared a positive update on Brandon Ingram heading into the weekend. Ingram revealed that he is now playing “full contact 5-on-5” and is getting closer to returning to game action, ClutchPoints’ Tomer Azarly reported. Ingram also said he will need more practice to keep building confidence in his recovering foot. item.title: Chiefs Legend Calls out Creed Humphrey for Errant Snaps
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 12: Center Creed Humphrey #52 of the Kansas City Chiefs in action during the game against the Detroit Lions at Arrowhead Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs‘ offensive line has been more of a problem than they expected this season. Left tackle Josh Simmons has yet to take the field as he continues to rehab from a bulging disc in his back. Taking his place has been rookie Kahili Benson, who has produced mixed results. Left guard Kingsley Suamataia has been benched twice this season, and center Creed Humphrey has struggled to snap the ball cleanly. Kansas City Chiefs Hall of Fame Center Tim Grunhard Calls Out Creed Humphrey for Errant Snaps @grunny61 talked about Kahlil Benson being the right tackle of the future & Creed Humphrey's snap issues with us on @ArrowheadAllies. pic.twitter.com/g1n2efxHuO — Starcade Media (@StarcadeMediaKC) November 5, 2026 Humphrey is a three-time All-Pro, making his issues with snapping the ball puzzling. Former Chiefs center Tim Grunhard, who was inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame in 2021, sounded off over Humphrey’s errant snaps while joining the folks at Starcade Media. “Communication is important, blocking the guy in front of you is important, finishing plays is important, but the most important thing is to get the ball to the damn quarterback,” Grunhard said. “That’s your job, it’s as simple as that. When you’re not doing it correctly, it’s like giving up a sack. It’s like having a missed assignment. It screws the play up. I’ve talked to him over the years. I’m sure he knows I’ve said it before. The reality is, your number one responsibility is to get the ball to the quarterback in a timely fashion.” Grunhard Praises Kahlil Benson Although Benson has had some struggles, he is doing better than most expected . Benson is an undrafted free agent, and did not play left tackle at all during his collegiate days. Grunhard believes Benson is doing fine at left tackle, and will be a great right tackle some day. “Kahlil Benson is the right tackle of the future for the Kansas City Chiefs,” Grunhard said. “I think he’s doing a nice job over at left tackle. As good as you can ask from him. He’s a right tackle. He’s more of a mauler, he’s a physical football player. I do think he struggles against some speed rushes, but he’s done a good job. He hung in there. You haven’t heard his name a lot, you haven’t heard his number a lot. If you don’t hear those two things, than an offensive lineman is doing ok.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Chiefs Legend Calls out Creed Humphrey for Errant Snaps appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: LaVell’s trust, confidence fueled Brandon Doman’s belief that he could win
item.description: BYU’s Brandon Doman goes head-to-head with Utah’s Arnold Parker during the Utah v. BYU game at Rice Eccles Stadium at the University of Utah on Friday, November 24, 2000. | JOHANNA WORKMAN Editor’s note: Eighth in an occasional series exploring LaVell Edwards’ legacy of leadership. No player who suited up for LaVell Edwards faced more immediate pressure to succeed than Brandon Doman. Injuries to the other quarterbacks opened the door for Doman to make his first start at BYU in the last home game for his legendary coach. Doman had dreamed of this opportunity ever since he was old enough to hold a football. He waited patiently for his moment — and it was finally here. “I had seen him put all of his effort and energy behind a quarterback before, and in that moment, I knew I had Lavell Edwards in my corner, and when he said, ‘You’re my guy,’ he was going to give me every shot,” Doman said. “So, I walked out of his office with the utmost confidence that he believed in me, and that I could go lead the football team. I don’t know that there’s any quarterback that played at BYU that’s walked out of his office, having been told, ‘You’re my guy,’ who didn’t feel that way.” Adding to the pressure of the moment, which included a pesky New Mexico team, was the fact that at 4-6, BYU was on the cusp of sending Edwards into retirement with his first losing season since 1972 — four years before his new quarterback was born. Doman needed to go 2-0 to keep that from happening. In addition, Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, stopped by the locker room to give the team a pregame pep talk that included his famous line: “Don’t muff it!” “I think when that moment occurred, the prophet was there, who I loved, President Hinckley, and Lavell Edwards. I mean, I can’t think of two more iconic people in the year 2000 for a member of the church than those two, and there we were, standing and surrounding them, shoulder to shoulder, and in kind of a sacred moment with the prophet, and also this, you know, war cry to go out and play the greatest game of all time. “I felt both the spirit and the power of calmness that it brought. I also felt like I was ready to go,” he continued. “And I’ve said this my whole life, because I was raised this way, and it’s a sacred thing to me, and I don’t know what other words to use for it, but I know it’s real and it draws emotion out of me — if your mind can conceive it and your heart can believe it, you can achieve it.” Bolstered by Edwards’ unyielding support, Doman marched the Cougars up and down the field. He led the team with 349 yards passing and 51 yards rushing, including an 8-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. BYU dominated the Lobos 37-13 and sent Edwards out of his final home game as a winner. item.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
item.description: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm , which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile , potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off. Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions. What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network? item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
item.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
item.description: null Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today . "This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added. Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites , which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite. BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9 , Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift. The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace , to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly. Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage. Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile. "The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement. The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement. Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. item.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. The protesters called on security agencies and state institutions to intervene and ensure a level playing field for all political parties. Another youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats or intimidation. “Opposition parties must be allowed to campaign safely, present their platforms, and engage with voters without constant threat of violence,” the coordinator said. The group said the march was part of efforts by young people in the state to demand accountability and promote peaceful political participation as the 2027 general elections approach. The post Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
item.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. It's not surprising to me that you can get to it, but how little effort you need to put into setting that up to get models to share anything.” The researchers tested nine models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Luna, and GPT-6.1-Sol, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. item.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. item.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
item.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide.
